## ICIP Workshop Proposal - Full Text Content

**ICIP Workshop Proposal.**

**Title:** Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling

**Workshop Organizers**

**Mourad Oussalah** is a full professor at University of Oulu, leading the social mining research group. He is involved in Finnish Research Council Digital Water flagship and Hybrid Intelligence flagship with notable work in applications of computer vision, machine learning and remote sensing technology to environment monitoring and prediction. He actively published in the field with more than 300 technical publications. He has also recently organized workshops at top conferences including CIKM'2025 and AAA-2026.
- University of Oulu, Finland, mourad.oussalah@oulu.fi

**Olof Mogren** is a research director at RISE Sweden, working on deep learning and foundational models with applications to climate adaptation and environment where he published in top venues such as ICCV, CVPR. He is actively involved in research commercialization and building as part of RISE core activities. He leads the Climate AI Nordic, a Nordic initiative for promoting the AI research in climate change and environment process monitoring.
- RISE Research Institute of Sweden, Olof.Mogren@ri.se

**Jukka Heikkonen** is a professor at Turku University and leads the Algorithms and Computational Intelligence Research Group. He is actively working at the intersection of computer vision and GIS data analysis, applied to geographical applications and autonomous systems, with more than 200 publications in the field. He is involved in Finland Research Council Digital Water flagship and several EU and national projects. Prof. Jukka also contributed to organization of several international conferences, e.g., ICANN, WITMSE, SCIA.
- University of Turku, jukhei@utu.fi

**Abstract**

Earth Observation is a rapidly growing research field that brings together computer vision, machine learning, and signal/image processing to provide valuable information about climate change, water cycle and predicting environmental attributes (e.g., water quality, snow depth, vegetation cover, pollution).

Recent advances in satellite observation analysis, discrepancy of on-site sensory modalities and land-surface modelling as well as availability of large scale datasets (e.g., Copernicus) together with growing pretrained models offer new opportunities for scalable, computational efficient, and observation-driven prediction suitable for operational and/or pre-operational use.

This workshop aims to bring together experts in machine vision, satellite observation, machine learning, remote sensing, hydrology and land-surface modelling to report on the latest findings on use of such technology for land-surface processes, water management and climate monitoring with varying spatial, temporal and spectral resolution. This implicitly fosters collaboration between Computer Vision, Remote Sensing and Environmental Monitoring communities, enhancing new computer vision based environmental research. This builds a bridge between several IEEE societies (e.g., GRSS, SPS, SSIT, CIS).

The workshop seeks contributions in the following categories:

**Methods:** Data-centric machine learning models for remote sensing data; language processing (such as Large Language Models, CLIP, Visual language models); data assimilation techniques for tackling discrepancy in image / time resolution; multi-modal approaches for parameter estimation / prediction; generative models (GANs, stable diffusion) for remote sensing; explainability and interpretability; super-resolution.

**Applications:** Disaster relief; urban planning; sustainable and intelligent agriculture; snow / water prediction; coast, sea, and marine monitoring; pollution monitoring; air/water quality analysis; climate change; geoscience; phenological studies.

**Open-data:** New open dataset for remote sensing applications; imaging annotated dataset for environmental analysis; optical and radar image dataset highlighting deep fake, noise and domain specialization.

**Composition**

The workshop is organized as a half day event, including:
- One Keynote speaker (45 minute presentation)
- A set of oral presentations (between 15 to 20 minutes for each presentation)
- A poster session, where each poster will be given an opportunity to make 5 minute ppt presentation
- A recognition of best paper/poster presentation

All the submissions will follow ICIP template and will be included in IEEExplore, with a set of selected papers to be submitted to post ICIP publication venues. A dynamic website that enables recording of number of visits and attracts interest from researchers wordwide.

**Duration:** Half-day
**Attendees:** 30-40 participants

**International Program Committee (tentative)**
- Sofoklis Kakouros (University of Oulu, Finland)
- Mehrdad Rostami (University of Oulu, Finland)
- Alexis Pirinen (RISE, Sweden)
- Timo Knuutila (University of Turku, Finland)
- Carlos Gonzales Inca (University of Oulu, Finland)
- Moncef Gabbouj (University of Tampere, Finland)
- Harri Kartinen (NLS, Finland)
- Kallasvuo Meri (LUKE, Finland)
- Bjorg Risebrobakken (Norce, Norway)
- Khalifa Djemel (University of Evry, France)
- Diego Marcos (INRIA, France)
- Suvojit Acharjee (Narula Institute of Technology, India)
- Sheli Sinha Chaudhuri (Jadavpur University, India)

**Additional sponsorship:** Digital Water flagship will help to sponsor Keynote speaker talk

**Workshop Proceedings:** IEEExplore
